subject: Deterministic SLA, vGPU packing & reservation workshop
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@cloudnova.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation questions — deterministic throughput needs

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the RFP follow-up. We reviewed the dedicated capacity section and have two immediate clarifications before our procurement review:

1) Deterministic SLA: CloudNova needs a 99.95% token-level availability for tail-latency under 300ms P95 for our customer-facing chat endpoint (30k qps peak, burst to 45k). Can Redwood guarantee latency SLOs across mixed workloads or do we need dedicated GPU families pinned per pool?

2) vGPU/packing: Our infra team wants to understand how you pack smaller models and multi-tenant vGPU slices — specifically whether you mix A100 and H100 in the same reserved pool and how that affects deterministic throughput.

I attached a small workload profile (cloudnova-workload-profile.csv) — it contains percentile request sizes and concurrency. Can someone from the capacity team complete the worksheet and share a short explanation we can hand to procurement?

Appreciate a short write-up and any sample packing rules. If easier, we can schedule a 30m workshop next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Procurement — CloudNova
[attachment: cloudnova-workload-profile.csv (text/csv)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation questions — deterministic throughput needs

Alex —

Thanks for the clear questions and the profile. I pasted quick answers below and attached a filled worksheet (redwood-dedicated-worksheet.xlsx). We should also do a short workshop to validate assumptions (I propose Mon, Dec 14).

Quick answers:
- Deterministic SLA: We target deterministic latency SLOs by isolating pools by latency class and enforcing request routing policies. For 300ms P95 at your load we recommend reserving a single-family pool (prefer H100-80GB) for the chat endpoint, with an autoscale buffer of ~15% for burst tolerance.

- Pool mixing: We do not recommend mixing A100 and H100 in the same logical reserved pool for deterministic SLAs. Mixing is supported for non-latency-critical workloads but leads to heterogeneous kernel paths and makes tail-latency guarantees weaker.

- vGPU packing: For multi-tenant vGPU slices, we use strict placement constraints: we only colocate compatible quantized model variants on the same physical card; otherwise we allocate whole-card instances. See the worksheet for the example packing rules and throughput per-GPU.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-worksheet.xlsx — includes modeled throughput (qps/token rate), expected token/sec per-GPU for H100/A100, and reservation sizing scenarios (reserved pool sizes for 30k/45k qps).

Next steps:
1) Review the worksheet and confirm which endpoints you want in the latency pool.
2) If you want, we can run a smoke test on a short canary (2–3 nodes) before full reservation provisioning.
3) Workshop to align on routing and fallback policies (Mon Dec 14 — I sent a calendar invite).

—Monica
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-dedicated-worksheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnova.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation questions — deterministic throughput needs

Alex / Monica —

Adding a couple of implementation details from capacity engineering so procurement has concrete numbers to review:

- GPU family throughput (approx, 8k token/sec model mix):
  * H100-80GB: ~18k tokens/sec (steady) / ~22k tokens/sec (burst optimized profile)
  * A100-80GB: ~12k tokens/sec (steady)

- Packing guidance for deterministic pools:
  * Reserve H100-only pool for the chat endpoint. Use container-level isolation (no overcommit) for latency-critical models.
  * If you need cost savings for background tasks (offline rerank/embeddings), put those in a mixed A100 pool with looser SLAs.
  * Reserve at least 1.2x headroom above modeled peak QPS to cover KV cache misses and short-term spikes.

- Canary/fallback plan: Spin up a 3-node H100 canary (same kernel/quantization profile) and run a 4-hour soak at 1.2x expected peak. If stable, promote to reserved pool. If not, we add a burst lane (pre-warmed) for 24–48 hours while we scale capacity.

Happy to walk through the worksheet in the workshop.

Ben
Staff Engineer, Capacity — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@cloudnova.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation questions — deterministic throughput needs

Monica / Ben —

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Can you confirm if the 1.2x headroom recommendation is included in the reservation commitment calculation or if it's expected to be covered by burst capacity (and billed separately)? Procurement needs to map to commit levels.

- For the canary test, we'd like an estimated cost delta (approx $/hour) for running the 3-node H100 canary and the incremental cost if burst lanes are used for 48 hours.

If you can add those two items to the worksheet, procurement will be able to finalize their preferred commit band. Also confirm any lead time (procurement -> reserved pool operational) — we have a hard start date of Jan 18, 2027 for the pilot.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex
Head of Procurement — CloudNova

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation questions — deterministic throughput needs

Alex —

Confirmed and updated:
- Headroom accounting: We recommend keeping the 1.2x headroom inside the reservation for predictable billing and deterministic SLAs. In the worksheet I added two reservation bands: "Commit+Headroom" and "Commit-only (burst)" so procurement can compare commit economics vs. burst-delta.

- Canary cost estimate: 3-node H100 canary ~ $85/hr (total). Burst lane incremental if used (48h) ~ $5,500 one-time incremental. I put these as ballpark numbers in the runbook.

- Lead time: Standard lead time for provisioning a reserved H100 pool is 7–10 business days after contract signature and capacity confirmation. For Jan 18 pilot start, we recommend signature by Jan 4 to allow provisioning and a 48h pre-pilot validation window.

I've attached a short reservation runbook (redwood-reservation-runbook-v1.pdf) that covers provisioning steps, canary runbook, rollback points, and a sample SLA addendum. Also included a calendar invite for the workshop on Mon Dec 14 10:00–10:30 PT with a link: https://calendar.example.com/meet/rdw-reservation-workshop-2026-12-14

If this looks good I'll update the worksheet with the exact commit bands once procurement confirms the preferred commit % (70/80/100).

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

—Monica
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
